clue.text: Difficult situation in wet low-lying ground

definitions.meaning: a ... figuratively is an awkward predicament hard to escape
literally a ... is a soft boggy area of land

explanation.surface: Someone stuck in a marsh is literally in a tough spot.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a bog and, by extension, a predicament one cannot easily get out of.

clue.text: Twelve-inch rung, it might be left in blanket covering the ground

definitions.text: it might be left in blanket covering the ground

parts.note: a foot is twelve inches long
a rung of a ladder is a step

explanation.surface: Sounds like a measuring note about a ladder, then a snowy scene.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'blanket covering the ground' is snow, in which a walker leaves prints.
explanation.definitionFit: A print of a foot is what a walker leaves behind in fresh snow.

clue.text: Drunk with two men taken along the way, unusually

parts.note: high means intoxicated
Jack and Ed are two men's names, side by side

explanation.surface: A tipsy pair of lads swept along a road, oddly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusually' flags the less common spelling of HIJACKED; a hijacker originally robbed travellers on the highway.
explanation.definitionFit: To hijack is to seize a vehicle or goods in transit, on the road.

clue.text: Feverish man about to have nervous twitch

parts.note: he is a male pronoun, so man
c, short for circa, means about
a tic is an involuntary nervous twitch

explanation.surface: A fevered man is about to develop a twitch.
explanation.definitionFit: Hectic originally described the flushed fever of consumption, now frantic activity.

clue.text: Equipment that's changed for hill-climbing?

definitions.meaning: a driver or cyclist shifts down a ... to climb a hill

explanation.surface: Asks what kit one swaps before tackling a slope.
explanation.definitionFit: Kit is called gear, and a vehicle's gear ratio is shifted on steep slopes.

clue.text: Weary end to game after squash rally

indicators.note: the weary and game pieces come after the squash piece

parts.note: to squash is to jam, press tightly
to weary someone is to bore them

indicators.note: end to signals the final letter of the word game

explanation.surface: A tired finish to a squash rally between two players.
explanation.walkthrough: 'squash' and 'rally' look like sport but squash means jam and rally is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A jamboree is a large festive gathering, as a rally is a mass meeting.

clue.text: Honest job applicants? Only sixty per cent

indicators.note: keeping only six of the ten letters means the last four are dropped

parts.note: candidates are people applying for a job

explanation.surface: Are applicants honest? Only a few of them, it seems.
explanation.walkthrough: CANDIDATES has ten letters; sixty per cent keeps the first six, dropping ATES.
explanation.definitionFit: Candid means frank and truthful, saying plainly what one thinks.

clue.text: In corner sat Zachary, substitute

indicators.note: in says the answer is found within the following words

explanation.surface: A substitute player named Zachary sat in the corner.
explanation.definitionFit: Ersatz describes an inferior replacement, an imitation standing in for the real thing.

clue.text: Four moving about, causing uproar

indicators.note: moving says the letters of four shift into a new order

parts.note: re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: Four people on the move create a commotion.
explanation.definitionFit: A furore is a public outburst of anger or excitement, much like a commotion.

clue.text: Warn maid with nosh cooked

indicators.note: cooked suggests the letters are messed about, as food is worked

explanation.surface: Telling off a maid over badly cooked food.
explanation.definitionFit: To admonish is to caution or reprimand someone firmly.

clue.text: Rabble-rouser with odd gait returning roster

indicators.note: odd suggests the word gait is set out in a strange order
returning means the word for roster is read backwards

parts.note: a rota is a roster of duties

explanation.surface: A troublemaker with a strange walk comes back to the duty list.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd' gives AGIT from GAIT, and 'returning' turns ROTA into ATOR.
explanation.definitionFit: An agitator stirs up crowds to protest, just as a rabble-rouser does.

clue.text: Drug operation I polished off

parts.note: to polish off food is to eat it, past tense ate

explanation.surface: After surgery, the patient finished off the painkillers.
explanation.definitionFit: An opiate is a narcotic derived from opium, such as morphine.

clue.text: Brick tiler crushed in very amusing story

indicators.note: crushed means the letters of the fodder are broken and reformed

explanation.surface: A tale of a tiler squashed by bricks somehow turns out hilarious.
explanation.definitionFit: A rib-tickler is a joke or tale so funny it makes one laugh hard.

clue.text: Beam when Sarah turns up with leading lady

indicators.note: in a down clue turns up means read the word from bottom to top

parts.note: Sal is a pet form of Sarah
ER, Elizabeth Regina, the Queen is the nation's leading lady

explanation.surface: Sarah beams when she arrives alongside the star actress.
explanation.definitionFit: A laser produces a narrow intense beam of light.

clue.text: Make a speedy apology?

parts.note: express can mean fast, as in an express train, so a fast apology

explanation.surface: Asks how one would say sorry quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means to say sorry; read literally as an adjective it means a sorry that is quick.

clue.text: Postholder?

parts.note: post is mail, and this item holds a letter; it reads like someone holding a job

explanation.walkthrough: 'Postholder' suggests someone in a job; here post means mail.
explanation.definitionFit: A paper sleeve holds a letter sent by mail, so it literally holds the post.

clue.text: Blue piece of music, perhaps

parts.note: Gershwin's famous work is titled in Blue; a sad song would be blue too

explanation.surface: A melancholy tune, or so it seems.
explanation.walkthrough: Gershwin's 'Rhapsody in Blue' is the piece meant.
explanation.definitionFit: A rhapsody is a free-form musical composition, exemplified by Gershwin's jazz-tinged work.

clue.text: Break in spring found in lock

indicators.note: found in says the spring word sits inside the lock word

parts.note: a tress is a lock of hair
a spa is a mineral spring

explanation.surface: A burglar breaks in by forcing the lock with a spring.
explanation.definitionFit: To trespass is to enter property unlawfully, to intrude on it.

clue.text: Away with learner in charge, resulting in playful behaviour

parts.note: fro means away, as in to and fro
L is for learner, as on a learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: With the learner left in charge, the trip turns into larking about.
explanation.definitionFit: A frolic is lively, carefree play or merriment.

clue.text: Representation in law but not third time

indicators.note: but not third says the third occurrence of the time letter is removed

parts.note: a statute is a written law

explanation.surface: Legal representation, but not on the third occasion.
explanation.walkthrough: STATUTE has three Ts; removing the third leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A statue is a sculpted figure that represents a person or thing.

clue.text: Was different entry included that was diversified in colour?

indicators.note: included says the entry word is taken inside the other

parts.note: varied means was different, changed
a gate is an entry point

explanation.surface: Asks whether an entry was colourful enough to stand out.
explanation.definitionFit: Variegated describes leaves or petals with patches of different colours.

clue.text: Pass by, do not start to deteriorate

indicators.note: do not start means the word loses its opening letter

parts.note: to relapse is to fall back into worse health

explanation.surface: Advice to a patient not to begin getting worse.
explanation.definitionFit: Time that elapses goes by, slips past.

clue.text: Feel acute embarrassment, His Excellency has court order first

indicators.note: first places the court order ahead of the title

parts.note: a writ is a written order from a court

explanation.surface: An ambassador squirms when served a court order.
explanation.definitionFit: To writhe is to twist in discomfort, here figuratively squirming with shame.

clue.text: Religious wing

parts.note: not a faction of a faith but a part of a church building

explanation.walkthrough: 'wing' suggests a faction of believers; it is architectural.
explanation.definitionFit: The transept is the cross-arm of a church, projecting either side of the nave.

clue.text: Inferior articles given a farewell

parts.note: tat is cheap shoddy goods

explanation.surface: Cheap goods handed over at a goodbye.
explanation.definitionFit: Ta-ta is an informal British way of saying goodbye.

clue.text: Appeal to restrict god's excess

indicators.note: to restrict says the appeal word closes around the god

parts.note: a plea is an appeal or request
Thor is the Norse god of thunder; the 's reads as is, linking to the definition

explanation.surface: A plea to curb divine extravagance.
explanation.definitionFit: A plethora is an overabundance, more than is needed.

clue.text: Lover of cruelty unhappy first

parts.note: sad means unhappy
1st, with the digit read as the letter I

explanation.surface: A cruel person is unhappy to come first.
explanation.definitionFit: A sadist takes pleasure in inflicting pain on others.

clue.text: Put one's foot down

parts.note: the idiom means to insist firmly, but a driver literally presses the pedal

explanation.walkthrough: The idiom suggests being firm; a driver's foot on the pedal speeds up.
explanation.definitionFit: Pressing the pedal to the floor makes a car go faster.
